description: Acceptance evidence for milestone W-A of docs/whole_space_transition.md: the exact modal transparent (Dirichlet-to-Neumann) outer condition d_r psi_hat_k(R) + [2/R + |k| K_0(|k|R)/K_1(|k|R)] psi_hat_k(R) = 0 applied to the E-25 finite-cylinder elliptic problem. The same compactly supported source family as the E-33 wall-truncation run (support 0.95, exponent 8, core 0.9) is solved on nested cylinders R in {1, 1.5, 2, 3} that share their radial spacing bitwise, under both outer conditions, at three radial resolutions, for one exactly z-independent case and three axial modes spanning kR from 0.196 (algebraic regime) to 6.28 (exponential regime).
equation: -(d_rr + 3/r d_r + d_zz) psi1 = omega1 with d_r psi_hat_k(R) + [2/R + |k| K_0(|k|R)/K_1(|k|R)] psi_hat_k(R) = 0
interpretation: This measures whether the transparent outer condition removes the artificial-wall truncation error of THIS discretization, leaving only the O(dr^2) discretization error of the boundary row. It is not a continuum bound, it does not make the elliptic problem a whole-space problem in any rigorous sense, and it is not singularity evidence. Its content is narrow: with a compactly supported source, moving the artificial wall stops moving the solution.
known_gaps: the 'no_curvature_term' fault is detected as a refusal rather than as a wrong number: dropping 2/R makes the k=0 modal matrix a singular discrete Neumann operator and the unpivoted elimination stops; the k>0 modes are measured separately through the single-mode path so that the fault also has a numerical detection factor

the 'frozen_ratio' fault (K_0/K_1 := 1) is invisible at k=0 by construction, because the bracket is 2/R there for both; it is detected only on the k>0 cases, and this experiment records that limitation as a measured bitwise identity rather than hiding it
no continuum error bound is produced anywhere; the whole bundle is a finite-dimensional consistency measurement

condition 4 compares against a Dirichlet solve at finite R_big, whose own wall error decays only algebraically for kR << 1; for the longest wavelength case the reference is therefore not converged and the split reports the wall term as dominant, which is the point of E-33 rather than a defect of the transparent condition
limitations: binary64 arithmetic without outward rounding; every tolerance below is a measured floating-point band, not a proof

(W-1) is exact only while omega_1 vanishes for r >= R; the discretized condition still carries an O(dr^2) boundary error, so 'R-independent' here means 'R-dependent only at the discretization level', never zero

the transparent condition is diagonal in the axial Fourier index and therefore nonlocal in z; it has no real-space z-stencil, so solver C cannot cross-validate it and the independent path used instead is the large-radius Dirichlet solve of condition 4
the radial profile (1-(r/a)^2)^p used for conditions 1, 2, 4 and 6 is compactly supported and C^(p-1), not C^infinity

the manufactured family of condition 3 is exactly the decaying branch A K_1(kr)/r outside its support, matched to an even sextic inside; it satisfies (W-1) identically at every R beyond the support, which is what makes the boundary row testable, but its source is only C^1 across the support edge
observed orders are computed over the listed grids only; they are not continuum error bounds
physical_wall_warning: The condition measured here belongs to the whole-space problem. The Hou reproduction keeps the PHYSICAL no-slip wall of audit entry E-27, where psi_1(t,1,z)=0 is a boundary condition of the modelled flow and not a truncation artefact. Runs that reproduce Hou must keep boundary_condition='dirichlet'; the transparent path exists only for whole-space exploration and is never selected implicitly.
